Finding_class: Verified source facts; architectural implication; unconfirmed defect hypothesis; missing tenant policy
Affected_workflow: Multi-company login context; EMS; assets; projects; leave; expenses; documents; dashboards
Observed_implementation_behavior: Membership context validates one active selected company, but multiple legacy domain records/queries are not consistently company-keyed or filtered.
Existing_safeguards: Company/session preference checks; active membership checks for scoped routes; modern Attendance uses company IDs and transaction context; registered-device RLS.
Risk_supporting_evidence: Global arrays/aggregations and privileged policies create plausible cross-company visibility or mutation paths when two companies coexist.
Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: Seed/mock data are disabled in declared production; some module tests scope specific reads; no deployed two-company execution evidence was obtained.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: Actual production topology/data composition and whether any super-tenant role is intended are unverified.
Potential_business_impact: Exposure or mutation of another company's personnel, financial, leave, asset, or document data; inaccurate empty workspace.
Severity_priority_rationale: Critical/P0 because confidentiality and integrity cross a tenant trust boundary, but this is not labeled a confirmed vulnerability without authorized execution.
Resolution_type: Product policy decision; engineering verification; authorized two-company testing
Proposed_QA_coverage: Build two populated companies plus empty company; exercise every role and object-ID substitution on list/detail/create/update/delete/export; verify both rows and side effects remain company-scoped.
Accountable_stakeholder: Product Owner and Engineering Lead / Architect

Finding_class: Verified source facts; unconfirmed authorization defect hypothesis; missing reporting policy
Affected_workflow: Reports; CSV/XLSX/PDF export; generated document download
Observed_implementation_behavior: Several report data sets aggregate global store collections; Admin/Auditor export authorization is broad; generated exports are persisted as document/storage objects.
Existing_safeguards: Role gates exist; report-row helpers restrict some employee views; export serialization includes spreadsheet-formula sanitization; generated export metadata is stored.
Risk_supporting_evidence: HR user report enumerates users globally, leave summary uses broad balance/holiday rows, audit combines global events, and privileged export check is not company-qualified.
Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: Some employee views use row-visibility helpers and role gates, so the authorization model is not uniformly global; no runtime disclosure was demonstrated.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: Whether any approved cross-company Auditor/Admin role exists, the production data mix, object-download ACLs and deployed route exposure are unverified.
Potential_business_impact: Bulk disclosure has higher blast radius than a single record and may corrupt company decisions or regulatory reporting.
Severity_priority_rationale: Critical/P0 due bulk data and privileged roles; source establishes exposure path candidates, not deployed exploitability.
Resolution_type: Product policy decision; engineering verification; authorized report/export testing
Proposed_QA_coverage: Two-company row/object matrix for every report and format; direct generated-document access; filter tampering; revoked/changed role; large export; formula payload; retention/expiry.

Finding_class: Verified deployment declaration; unverified deployment hypothesis; missing operational acceptance criterion
Affected_workflow: Signup verification; password setup/reset; transactional notifications
Observed_implementation_behavior: The committed Render blueprint declares EMAIL_DELIVERY_MODE=disabled while auth creates verification/reset tokens and delivery records.
Existing_safeguards: Tokens are purpose-bound/expiring; email delivery has source-level contract tests and non-production modes; hosted UI has confirmation behavior.
Risk_supporting_evidence: A disabled declared mode would prevent real recipient delivery even though API token generation succeeds.
Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: Application-owned token controls, delivery telemetry, hosted confirmation UX and email-focused test source reduce risk in the implementation layer.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: The live service may override the blueprint; provider credentials, sender/domain verification, queues, webhooks, deliverability and monitoring were not inspected.
Potential_business_impact: Users cannot activate accounts or recover passwords; support and onboarding stoppage.
Severity_priority_rationale: Critical/P0 because core access depends on email, with high likelihood in the declared configuration but no live-environment confirmation.
Proposed_QA_coverage: Inspect effective config and provider health; end-to-end delivery for signup/reset; expiry/replay/wrong-purpose; provider timeout/retry/bounce; verify no tokens leak in hosted response/logs.

Finding_class: Verified source facts; architectural implication; unconfirmed concurrency defect hypothesis
Observed_implementation_behavior: Most domains mutate a process-local hydrated store and flush selected domains in onSend; each process loads its own snapshot. Attendance routes are explicitly transaction-owned.
Existing_safeguards: PostgreSQL flush is transactional; versions/OCC exist in several records; one-process deployment would serialize local state; Attendance avoids this architecture.
Risk_supporting_evidence: No repository-wide refresh/pub-sub/locking mechanism was found to reconcile independent API snapshots; post-response/onSend persistence can fail after handler logic.
Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: A hard single-writer deployment plus domain OCC would materially reduce this risk; Attendance already avoids the hydrated command pattern.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: API instance count, autoscaling, rolling-deploy overlap, request affinity and accepted per-domain staleness/loss are unverified.
Potential_business_impact: Lost updates, stale authorization/role reads, overwritten records, non-repeatable workflow decisions.
Severity_priority_rationale: Critical/P0 if more than one writer exists or restarts overlap; lower if a single controlled writer is a hard invariant.
Resolution_type: Architectural engineering verification; topology decision; authorized concurrency/failure testing
Proposed_QA_coverage: Same-record and different-record concurrent writes from two instances; stale role/deactivation; flush failure; restart during mutation; OCC behavior by domain; measure lost/duplicate side effects.
Accountable_stakeholder: Engineering Lead / Architect and Platform / SRE

Finding_class: Verified source facts; unconfirmed authorization defect hypothesis; missing business policy
Observed_implementation_behavior: Document policy allows Admin or Auditor to read and mutate/verify/delete broadly; records are not visibly tenant-qualified. Expense attachment accepts a verified document without an evident ticket-access check in that method.
Existing_safeguards: All calls still require authenticated role checks; upload validation/checksum and UI delete confirmation exist; generic Auditor auth permission map is read-oriented.
Risk_supporting_evidence: Module policy's write/delete allowance conflicts with the read-only description and tenant isolation intent; object-ID based methods make ownership important.
Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: All routes remain authenticated, upload validation and delete confirmation exist, and the general Auditor permission map is read-oriented.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: Intended Auditor mutation and company scope, route-level narrowing and deployed object-ID reachability are unapproved or untested.
Potential_business_impact: Unauthorized deletion, verification or association of HR/legal/financial documents; audit/compliance harm.
Severity_priority_rationale: Critical/P0 because documents are sensitive and destructive mutation is possible in source, but exploitability remains unverified.
Resolution_type: Security/product decision; engineering verification; authorized negative testing
Proposed_QA_coverage: Role/action/tenant/object matrix including Auditor; guessed IDs; deleted/verified/legal/finance classes; attach foreign document to expense; direct storage/download; audit trail.

Finding_class: Verified source facts; architectural implication; unconfirmed failure defect hypothesis
Observed_implementation_behavior: Upload writes object storage before metadata/outbox persistence; delete removes storage before SQL/memory deletion; generated export similarly uploads before metadata.
Existing_safeguards: SQL metadata mutations are grouped in transactions in persistence paths; checksums/object keys and audit/outbox records exist; production mock storage is rejected.
Risk_supporting_evidence: Database and external object storage cannot share the SQL transaction, so crashes/errors can leave orphan objects or metadata referring to missing content.
Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: No observed orphan or missing-object incident is evidenced; SQL portions roll back and stable object/checksum metadata can support repair.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: Provider idempotency/lifecycle, object-key reuse, reconciliation jobs, alerts and operator recovery procedures are unverified.
Potential_business_impact: Orphaned confidential objects, broken downloads, inconsistent audit, repeated charges/storage growth, irreversible loss on delete.
Severity_priority_rationale: High/P1 because partial failures are realistic and deletion can be irreversible; blast radius is usually per object.
Resolution_type: Engineering verification; privacy retention decision; authorized fault-injection testing
Proposed_QA_coverage: Inject storage success/DB failure and storage failure/DB success at each boundary; retry same request; reconciliation/alerting; legal-hold class; export cleanup.
Accountable_stakeholder: Engineering Lead / Architect and Security / Privacy

Finding_class: Verified source facts; unconfirmed session-control defect hypothesis; missing deactivation semantics
Affected_workflow: Employee deactivation; role change; login disablement; existing browser/bearer session
Observed_implementation_behavior: Core deactivation and login-disable are distinct paths; disable-login revokes user sessions, while deactivation does not visibly call the session-store revocation method. Auth actor check rejects deleted users but not every inactive employment state.
Existing_safeguards: Explicit revokeUser exists; logout and disable-login use revocation; company membership context can require active employment for scoped routes; roles are resolved from current actor data.
Risk_supporting_evidence: An existing session may remain usable on routes that do not require active employment after a deactivation-only action.
Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: The explicit login-disable path revokes user sessions, logout/reset have revocation controls, and selected membership contexts require active employment.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: HR may always combine deactivation with login disablement; session TTL, Valkey consistency and route adoption of active-employment checks are unverified.
Potential_business_impact: Former employee retains access or privileges persist after role change; privacy and fraud exposure.
Severity_priority_rationale: High/P1 because lifecycle revocation is a common control; risk depends on approved offboarding orchestration.
Resolution_type: Security/product decision; engineering verification; authorized lifecycle testing
Proposed_QA_coverage: Login then deactivate/terminate/disable/change role; reuse cookie and bearer across every module; multi-instance and Valkey outage; verify audit and immediate/defined-delay revocation.

Finding_class: Verified source facts; architectural implication; unconfirmed governance defect hypothesis; missing finance rules
Affected_workflow: Expense submit; manager verification; finance approval; payment; settlement; backup routing
Observed_implementation_behavior: Requester self-processing is denied; assigned manager and finance reviews are separate and backup configuration exists. No universal minimum two-person staffing or clear attachment authorization in attachVerifiedDocument was found.
Existing_safeguards: State transitions validate role/assignment/status and use version fields in key paths; money utility uses integer cents; integration tests cover standard flow and backup cases.
Risk_supporting_evidence: Combined roles, missing eligible backup, concurrent transitions, payment/settlement variance and attachment association could violate unapproved four-eyes expectations.
Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: Self-processing denial, assigned approvers, backups, state/version checks and standard-flow test source materially reduce common-path risk.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: Deployed staff assignments, combined-role rules, amount-change authority, accounting integration and routing-exception policy are unverified.
Potential_business_impact: Fraud, stuck reimbursements, double/incorrect payment, incomplete audit or policy breach.
Severity_priority_rationale: Critical/P0 for financial integrity; priority cannot be retired by happy-path automation alone.
Resolution_type: Finance business decision; engineering verification; authorized state/concurrency testing
Proposed_QA_coverage: Decision table across role combinations and backups; self/peer actions; duplicate/concurrent transitions; stale version; amount/currency variance; foreign attachment; reject/resubmit; payment/settlement audit.

Finding_class: Verified source facts; unconfirmed calculation/scoping defect hypothesis; missing HR rules
Affected_workflow: Leave request duration; balance; holidays by company/region/optional status
Observed_implementation_behavior: Holiday management calls resolve actor company, but entitlement/calculation selects broad policy/company/holiday collections and does not visibly apply employee region or optional-holiday choice.
Existing_safeguards: Holiday records carry region/optional fields; actor company is used on management writes; request and balance lifecycle exists.
Risk_supporting_evidence: First-active/global selection and broad holiday rows can apply another company's calendar or wrong region when multiple configurations exist.
Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: Holiday writes resolve actor company and records preserve region/optional fields, providing data needed for a corrected or more specific calculation.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: A single-company deployment may mask the issue; approved regional/optional rules, accrual formulas and actual tenant data are unknown.
Potential_business_impact: Wrong leave deduction/balance, attendance conflict, payroll or employee-relations disputes.
Severity_priority_rationale: High/P1 because calculation errors accumulate and affect many employees; exact defect status needs multi-company execution and policy.
Resolution_type: HR business decision; engineering verification; authorized boundary testing
Proposed_QA_coverage: Two companies with overlapping/different holidays; employee regions; optional selection; half day; weekend; cross-year/leap year; timezone; negative/insufficient balance; concurrency.

Finding_class: Verified source facts; unconfirmed date/projection defect hypothesis; missing payroll correction policy
Affected_workflow: Cross-midnight attendance; offline punch; regularization; auto-punchout; payroll lock/adjustment
Observed_implementation_behavior: Server derives work date; open session retains start date, but some projection/outbox work uses a current work date. Regularization requires item timestamps to match requested local date. Payroll lock snapshots data and stores post-lock adjustments.
Existing_safeguards: Attendance commands use SQL transactions, advisory locks, idempotency, sequence/device/company validation; cross-midnight shift resolver and auto-punchout have focused tests; payroll snapshots preserve history.
Risk_supporting_evidence: A night checkout/regularization may land on a different projection day; no route resolving post-lock adjustments was located.
Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: Direct SQL transactions, idempotency, locks, immutable snapshots and focused regularization/worker test source reduce corruption and duplicate risk.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: Canonical work date, supported timezones/DST, client clock trust and how pending adjustments are approved/applied are unresolved.
Potential_business_impact: Incorrect hours/overtime/absence, rejected legitimate correction, payroll under/overpayment.
Severity_priority_rationale: High/P1 due payroll impact and complex boundary conditions; transactional safeguards materially reduce duplicate/corruption risk.
Resolution_type: HR/payroll decision; engineering verification; authorized temporal testing
Proposed_QA_coverage: Check-in before midnight and checkout after; multiple zones/DST; offline replay after midnight; auto-punchout; break spanning day; regularization; lock then approve correction; report/payroll reconciliation.
Accountable_stakeholder: HR / Payroll and Engineering Lead / Architect

Finding_class: Verified source facts; architectural implication; unconfirmed duplicate/loss hypothesis
Affected_workflow: Transactional outbox publish; downstream event consumption; retry/dead letter
Observed_implementation_behavior: Worker locks pending rows, publishes to Valkey stream, then marks SQL row processed and commits; failures retry and dead-letter after a threshold. The ADR defines at-least-once delivery and consumer-side dedupe.
Existing_safeguards: Database row locking, retry scheduling, dead-letter status, stable event IDs, and attendance atomic outbox writes exist; worker tests cover several safe-error/idempotency paths.
Risk_supporting_evidence: A crash after XADD but before SQL commit can republish; no downstream consumer/dedupe implementation or dead-letter replay operation was found in this repository.
Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: Stable event IDs, row locks, retry/dead-letter states and an explicit consumer-deduplication ADR reduce the intended at-least-once risk.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: Consumers may live outside this repository and dedupe correctly; Valkey durability/retention, alerts and dead-letter replay operations are unverified.
Potential_business_impact: Duplicate emails/actions, missing integrations, permanently stranded events, audit discrepancies.
Severity_priority_rationale: High/P1 because at-least-once is intentional but end-to-end correctness depends on unobserved consumers and operations.
Proposed_QA_coverage: Crash boundary after publish; same event redelivery; consumer dedupe by consumer/event; Valkey disconnect/reconnect; retry ceiling; DLQ alert/replay; stream trimming/restart.
Accountable_stakeholder: Platform / SRE and Engineering Lead / Architect

Finding_class: Verified source facts; unconfirmed deployment/integration hypothesis
Affected_workflow: Authenticated Vercel SSR deep link; refresh; cookie session; client hydration
Observed_implementation_behavior: Protected-shell redirect runs in client effect; shared API helper only uses browser credentials/session behavior; build smoke opens /login rather than an authenticated nested route.
Existing_safeguards: Client-side session fetch and redirects exist; production E2E and Playwright specs exercise routes in local/mocked contexts; Vercel configuration uses TanStack Start SSR output.

Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: Local client navigation specs, unauthenticated redirects and backend cookie/bearer contracts reduce risk for non-hosted and client-navigation paths.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: Actual Vercel routing/runtime, frontend/API origins, cookie attributes, edge behavior and intended server-versus-client auth design are unverified.
Potential_business_impact: Authenticated bookmarks/refreshed deep links fail, redirect loops, content flash or inconsistent access UX.
Severity_priority_rationale: High/P1 because all protected routes may be affected, but source alone cannot prove deployed failure.
Resolution_type: Engineering/deployment verification; authorized hosted browser testing
Proposed_QA_coverage: Direct URL/refresh/back-forward for every protected role; expired/stale cookies; API origin; SSR response vs hydrated DOM; 404 rewrites; multi-tab logout; slow network.
Accountable_stakeholder: Engineering Lead / Architect and Platform / SRE

Finding_class: Verified source facts; architectural implication; unconfirmed operational hypothesis
Affected_workflow: Outbox delivery; coordinate purge; attendance auto-punchout in shared worker
Observed_implementation_behavior: One separately deployed worker process schedules outbox, coordinate purge and auto-punchout loops; tasks are invoked sequentially within the loop and errors are caught/logged.
Existing_safeguards: Each task has its own error handling/interval; attendance auto-punchout uses locks and strong unit/integration coverage; worker is separate from API.
Risk_supporting_evidence: A slow/hung responsibility can delay later work; shared process crash/restart or resource saturation affects all three operational duties.
Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: Per-task catches, attendance locks/idempotency and a separately deployed worker reduce immediate API impact and support safe retry.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: Render supervision, health checks, task timeouts, instance count, CPU/memory, backlog volume, alerting and SLOs are unverified.
Potential_business_impact: Delayed events, retained precise location data, unclosed shifts, payroll/reporting lag.
Severity_priority_rationale: High/P1 because correlated failure spans compliance and payroll; likelihood depends on supervision and load.
Proposed_QA_coverage: Per-task hang/error/latency; process kill/restart; backlog catch-up; fairness; lock contention; resource saturation; alert thresholds; retention SLA.

Finding_class: Verified source facts; missing requirement; architectural implication; unconfirmed compliance defect hypothesis
Affected_workflow: Document/access logs; email payloads; exports; exact attendance coordinates; user data erasure
Observed_implementation_behavior: The system stores sensitive HR documents, audit/access events, export objects and location evidence; a coordinate purge worker and logger redaction exist, but no comprehensive class-by-class retention schedule was found.
Existing_safeguards: Exact-coordinate access is permission/audit controlled; coordinate purge exists; structured logging redacts session/password/token-like fields; document deletion and export metadata exist.
Risk_supporting_evidence: Other sensitive classes lack visible expiry/erasure/legal-hold rules; storage-first deletion can leave orphans; exported copies increase data footprint.
Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: Coordinate purge, exact-location access audit, logger redaction and document audit controls reduce exposure for selected data classes.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: Applicable jurisdictions/contracts, class-specific retention, backup deletion, legal hold, DSAR and Cloudinary lifecycle requirements are unknown.
Potential_business_impact: Regulatory/noncompliance exposure, excessive sensitive-data retention, inability to honor legal hold or erasure.
Severity_priority_rationale: High/P1 because HR, financial and location data are sensitive; compliance severity depends on jurisdiction and approved policy.
Resolution_type: Security/privacy business decision; engineering/deployment verification; authorized retention testing
Proposed_QA_coverage: Data inventory and retention per class; legal hold; employee deletion/DSAR; logs/backups/object versions; coordinate purge timing; export expiry; audit immutability; redaction negative cases.

Finding_class: Verified source facts; missing release process; unconfirmed deployment hypothesis
Affected_workflow: Release branch CI; promotion to Render/Vercel; migrations; rollback
Observed_implementation_behavior: release-* branches enter CI but deployment selection permits only named dev/qa/main branches; API production pre-deploy runs migrations; client smoke is limited to /login.
Existing_safeguards: Unsupported deployment branch fails closed; API and client have build/type/test jobs in workflow source; migrations are versioned; production mock/seed safeguards are declared.
Risk_supporting_evidence: There is no source-evident mapping of release-01 commit to a promoted immutable deployment, rollback compatibility gate, authenticated SSR smoke, or data restore drill.
Risk_reducing_or_contradictory_evidence: Unsupported deploy branches fail closed; migrations are versioned; declared production config disables mock/seed behavior.
Assumptions_and_unverified_conditions: External branch protections, approvals, immutable artifacts, environment overrides, backup/restore and manual promotion controls may exist but were not inspected.
Potential_business_impact: Wrong commit/config deployed, irreversible migration/rollback failure, release evidence not attributable to baseline.
Severity_priority_rationale: Medium/P2 initially, elevated to P1 for gate evidence because release identity and rollback are prerequisites for meaningful assurance.
Resolution_type: Deployment/process verification; QA gate decision; authorized release rehearsal
Proposed_QA_coverage: Prove commit/artifact identity; branch promotion; migration preflight/backward compatibility; failed migration rollback; Vercel/API config parity; backup restore; authenticated smoke; audit approvals.
